title: On the knot's spaces, junctions are paid for by atoms
subject: Whether counting on the knot's spaces is fixed-parameter tractable in the number of Fano atoms
conclusion: For every simple Pfaffian cubic bipartite graph other than the Heawood graph and every Pfaffian signing sigma, its Robertson-Seymour-Thomas junctions J, planar braces p and Heawood braces a satisfy J + p <= a + |sigma| - 2, attained by the trisum of three cubes with three edge atoms. So on hypergraphs not 2-colourable without signs every weighted colouring count takes time poly(n) 2^(a-2), while on Pfaffian systems in general counting is #P-hard with no Heawood brace.
